sn12.55:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases.
sn12.55:1.5: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.55:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree,
sn12.55:2.2: and all its roots going downwards and across would send the sap upwards.
sn12.55:2.3: Sustained by that sap, nourished by it, that great tree would stand for a very long time.
sn12.55:2.4: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases….
sn12.55:2.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.55:3.1: “When, bhikkhus, one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases.
sn12.55:3.2: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging….
sn12.55:3.4: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.55:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree.
sn12.55:4.2: Then a man would come along bringing a shovel and a basket.
sn12.55:4.3: He would cut down the tree at its foot, dig it up, and pull out the roots, even the fine rootlets and root-fibre.
sn12.55:4.4: He would cut the tree into pieces, split the pieces, and reduce them to slivers. Then he would dry the slivers in the wind and sun, burn them in a fire, and collect the ashes. Having done so, he would winnow the ashes in a strong wind or let them be carried away by the swift current of a river.
sn12.55:4.6: Thus that great tree would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no more subject to future arising.
sn12.55:4.7: “So too, bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to,
sn12.55:4.10: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
